items.title: Flat essentially finite type algebras and modules over a valuation ring are essentially of finite presentation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that over a valuation ring, a flat local homomorphism which is essentially of finite type is essentially of finite presentation, and that a finite module which is flat over the valuation ring is finitely presented over its algebra. The proof writes the algebra as a quotient of a localised polynomial algebra, chooses a presentation of the module over that localisation, and takes the intersection of the kernel with the polynomial algebra. That intersection localises back to the kernel, and the quotient it defines is a submodule of the module, hence flat over the valuation ring by torsion freeness, which combined with finiteness gives finite presentation over the polynomial algebra; exactness of localisation then identifies the localised submodule with the module.
